  > of additional data; used for version-tolerant analytics.
- `source`
  > What triggered/logged the event (user, system, automated job, integration
  > name); used for analytics and security audit.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the event was logged. Indexed for timeline/retention
  > queries.
- `updated_at`
  > Last update time of the event record (rarely modified except for error
  > correction or audit trail).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion marker; null if record is active. Used for retention and
  > legal hold.

### `political_economic_board_metrics`

Stores aggregated or point-in-time analytics metrics (e.g., MAU, DAU,
post_counts, report_counts, median_moderation_time) supporting platform
health dashboards, KPI tracking, and business analysis. Each metric is
associated with a name, value, window, and time granularity. Key for
longitudinal studies, performance reporting, and business success
evaluation. Metrics should be filtered and aggregated by name, window,
and time. Referential integrity with period-specific owners is possible
via nullable foreign keys.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `owner_member_id`
  > Metric calculated for a specific member's {@link
  > political_economic_board_members.id} actions, if applicable (e.g., user
  > retention, activity rates).
- `owner_moderator_id`
  > Metric calculated for a specific moderator's {@link
  > political_economic_board_moderators.id} performance or behavior.
- `owner_admin_id`
  > Metric tied to an admin's {@link
  > political_economic_board_administrators.id} period (for admin-related
  > analytics).
- `metric_name`
  > Business label for the metric (e.g., 'dau', 'mau', 'median_mod_time',
  > 'posts_today', 'post_quality_score'). Used in dashboards and analytics.
- `metric_value`
  > Value of the metric; semantic depends on name but always represents a
  > quantitative measurement available for statistics/KPI reporting.
- `window_start`
  > Time window start for the metric value (e.g., midnight for daily, first
  > of month for monthly metrics). For point-in-time metrics use created_at.
- `window_end`
  > Time window end for the metric value; same as window_start for
  > snapshot/instantaneous metrics.
- `granularity`
  > Resolution of the metric (daily, weekly, monthly, real_time, etc.); used
  > for aggregation/rollup in dashboards. Strongly affects analytics queries.
- `notes`
  > Optional detailed description, policy, calculation method, or comments
  > about metric context. Documentation/audit support.
- `created_at`
  > When the metric record was first written (for versioned or rolling
  > metrics, this is recalculated or retracked for new windows).
- `updated_at`
  > Last modification time for the metric (e.g., re-computed for correction
  > or business rule update).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete marker for expired/obsolete metrics (retained for audit and
  > rollback).

### `political_economic_board_data_anomalies`

Tracks analytics, engagement, or system anomalies that may signal data
quality issues, security events, business process exceptions, or
unexpected user/system behavior. Used for business incident triage,
process improvement, and compliance monitoring. Supports triage,
investigation, assignment, and resolution tracking for all anomaly
entries. Supports full-text search for anomaly type, description, and
context information.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `detected_by_member_id`
  > User (member) [political_economic_board_members.id](#political_economic_board_members) who reported or
  > detected the anomaly, if applicable.
- `detected_by_moderator_id`
  > Moderator [political_economic_board_moderators.id](#political_economic_board_moderators) who reported the
  > anomaly.
- `detected_by_admin_id`
  > Admin [political_economic_board_administrators.id](#political_economic_board_administrators) who flagged or
  > confirmed the anomaly.
- `anomaly_type`
  > Category of anomaly (e.g., data_inconsistency, metrics_spike,
  > missing_event, moderation_delay, duplicate_action, kpi_drop,
  > suspicious_activity, integration_failure). Supports reporting and
  > filtering.
- `anomaly_status`
  > Current resolution state (open, in_progress, resolved, false_positive,
  > ignored); business process triage status for workflow.
- `anomaly_description`
  > Human-readable description of anomaly context, impact, and known data.
  > Supports dashboarding, audit, search, and recall.
- `resolution_notes`
  > Documentation of investigation steps, findings, explanation, resolution
  > actions. Fully auditable for compliance.
- `detected_at`
  > Time the anomaly was detected (for automated/real-time, usually the
  > incident trigger time).
- `resolved_at`
  > Time anomaly was resolved or marked no-action (can be null if
  > unresolved/ongoing).
- `created_at`: When the anomaly entry was persisted for audit trail and process tracking.
- `updated_at`
  > Last time this anomaly or its status/notes changed; used for monitoring
  > and compliance.
- `deleted_at`
  > If non-null, the anomaly is soft-deleted or under legal hold. Used for
  > retention review.

### `political_economic_board_moderation_provider_logs`

Stores detailed logs of all interactions and payloads exchanged with
third-party content moderation providers for auditing, monitoring, and
compliance within the politicalEconomicBoard platform. Records provider,
request/response payloads, statuses, errors, and reference to the
high-level moderation action or report if available. This table enables
precise troubleshooting, quality assurance, and dispute handling for
moderation events, with typical queries by moderation action, provider,
or status.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `political_economic_board_reports_id`
  > Reference to the triggering report's {@link
  > political_economic_board_reports.id}.
- `provider`
  > Name or identifier of the third-party moderation provider servicing this
  > API call (e.g., 'OpenAI', 'AWS Comprehend').
- `request_payload`
  > Full raw payload sent to the provider, stored as JSON string for audit
  > tracing.
- `response_payload`
  > Full raw response received from the provider, stored as JSON string for
  > compliance and debugging.
- `status`: Status of the provider interaction (e.g., 'success', 'error', 'timeout').
- `error_message`
  > Full error message or exception information if the provider call failed.
  > Null if no error occurred.
- `external_reference_id`
  > External reference/correlation ID returned by the provider for
  > tracing/debugging. Null if unavailable.
- `created_at`: Timestamp this log entry was created (provider call initiation).
- `updated_at`: Last time this log was updated (e.g., status or error detail added).

### `political_economic_board_notification_provider_logs`

Comprehensive log table for all notification interactions with
third-party messaging providers (email, SMS, push) from the
politicalEconomicBoard. Tracks outgoing notification attempts, provider
responses, delivery status, errors, and allows tracing via notification
reference. Supports transparent audit, troubleshooting notification
issues, and monitoring provider reliability. Indexed for provider,
status, and timestamp for performance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `political_economic_board_notifications_id`
  > Reference to the dispatched notification's {@link
  > political_economic_board_notifications.id}.
- `provider`
  > Name or identifier of the messaging provider used for notification (e.g.,
  > 'SendGrid', 'Twilio', 'APNs').
- `request_payload`
  > Full JSON payload sent to provider (e.g., message body, to/address), for
  > audit/debug.
- `response_payload`
  > Full JSON response from provider (including any metadata, delivery
  > receipts).
- `status`
  > Provider transaction status (e.g., 'sent', 'delivered', 'failed',
  > 'queued').
- `error_message`: Error message/content, if any, for failed attempts. Null if successful.
- `external_reference_id`
  > Provider-assigned message or correlation ID for cross-referencing. Null
  > if unavailable.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when this log record was created (notification send attempt).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update (e.g., final delivery status).

### `political_economic_board_external_api_logs`

Centralized log for all third-party API calls (analytics, SSO, research
APIs, integrations) initiated from the politicalEconomicBoard platform,
for compliance, investigation, and support. Stores API provider details,
endpoint, request/response payloads, status, error detail, and external
transaction/correlation identifiers where available. Timely and
well-indexed for troubleshooting and governance. Generic enough to
accommodate new API integrations without schema change.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider`
  > Vendor or API provider name (e.g., 'Google Analytics', 'Okta SSO',
  > 'ModerationAI').
- `api_endpoint`
  > Identifies the API method, endpoint, or path invoked (e.g., '/analyze',
  > '/login').
- `request_payload`
  > JSON string of the request sent to the API (for later investigation or
  > support).
- `response_payload`
  > JSON string of the response received from the API (complete trace for
  > auditing).
- `status`: API call status (e.g., 'success', 'failed', 'delayed').
- `error_message`
  > Error message, if any, received from the external API. Null if
  > successful/no error.
- `external_reference_id`
  > Third-party correlation or transaction code for this API call. Null if
  > unavailable.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of log record creation (call attempt).
- `updated_at`
  > Last update to the log record (e.g., after a delayed status or error
  > reported).
